stage: R13a: a signed header the walk lexes from its line's start (a % on the line of its number), told by the digits past its run of signs (maintainer's answer R13-Q0)
commits: a93e60a fix: look for the digits a reading found past the signs of a header found at its first sign (pushed). Adds the private static PdfFileReader.DigitsPastSigns(span, spanStart, at). It gives the first byte at or past the place that is no sign, using IndexOfAnyExcept('+','-') over the window from the place, and gives the place itself where the run reaches the end of the bytes searched. The reached test becomes `candidate == absolute || (candidate != takeAt && (_sectionsReadAt.Contains(candidate) || _sectionDigitsAt.Contains(DigitsPastSigns(window.Memory.Span, start - lead, candidate))))`. The commit also carries the helper's XML doc and the rewritten comment above the reached test: the comment-line case leaves #332, and #332 keeps a reading inside the digits past the first. Refs #188, #327.
3aa09c3 test: pin a stream reached past its header's first sign not taken again where a % is on its line (pushed). Refs #188, #327.

dfb03fc docs: say a header found at its first sign is told by the digits past its signs (pushed). Source texts changed: the _sectionDigitsAt summary, the TryRelocateXRefSection remark (one overlong paragraph from a7bcdc6 wrapped again), and HeaderTokenStart's summary and remark. XRefSectionRecord.DigitsAt's summary changed too. Pages changed: threat-model.md row 449 (missing section tried at many places), its evidence column (the two new theories cited after the far theory) and the #327 Known gaps entry; diagnostics.md rows 110 and 111; lazy-reading.md around line 193. measurements: Reproduced on 69731a2 before any change. ZzR12gProbe's output equals round 12's g-head.txt byte for byte, MinusSigns included. My probe covered 220 blocks: 22 headers, in reach (past 30) and out of reach (past 511 to 514), readable and lost. It showed every '+'-started run with a % reached at a later sign or at the digit loop: readable gives offset-adjusted at the first sign, chain-cycle, rebuilt at opening and Error chain-loop; lost gives section-unreadable twice, Error section-malformed twice and chain-loop. That holds in reach and out of reach at past 511 and 512. The R12g reproducers c-pp-i1-ok and c-pp-i1-lost read as round 12 recorded.

After the fix, exactly 30 of the 220 probe blocks change: the % rows ('++5', '+5', '+++5') reached at a later sign or at the digit, near and far at past 511 and 512. The other 190 are byte-identical. Unchanged among them: the first-sign controls, '+-5 %c', '5 0 %c', a comment on its own line ('++5 0\n%c\nobj'), every twin without the %, and the far rows at past 513 and 514. In those far rows the % header is not found at all, its token starting before the bytes searched, as before. In ZzR12gProbe only the two 'near ++5 0 %c into=1' blocks change; its 58 other blocks and MinusSigns are unchanged.

The line test and the passed-over record need no widening for this shape, so they are unchanged. After the fix every '+'-started % row, readable and lost, near and far at 511 to 514, gives a block byte-identical to its twin without the %. That covers sections, opening diagnostics, objects 1 to 8, later reports, warnings and errors, newest offset normalized. No doubled or false report is left. For a lexed header, the line test is already asked at the token start, which is the place. The record of a stream passed over is made at that token start, and its look covers the whole number (StartsWithin to NumberEnd), so it already counts a section reached at a later sign or at the digit.

'-+5 0 %c' read at its '+' reads as its twin '-+5 0 obj' in sections, opening diagnostics, WasRepaired and objects 3, 4 and 7. It differs only in object 5, the stream's own row, which names the '-'. On the twin, the search near a row serves the header at its digit (Warning entry-shifted), the gap #327 already keeps. With the %, the walk lexes -5, so object 5 is null and the validator gives Error entry-broken; main does the same with the %.

deviations: New theories instead of extending b711d56's three. Their names would not stay true of every row: a row reached at the digit is not 'at its header or a sign of its number', and the readable near theory asserts no Error, which the '-+5 %c' row breaks (entry-broken for the stream's own row). The '-+5 %c' rows got a theory of their own because they cannot be 'read the same' as their twin in the validator: the twin's row is served at its digit by the search near a row, the gap #327 keeps.

'Controls: ... the % twins reached at the digit' was read as the twins written without the %, reached at the digit. The % files reached at the digit loop on 69731a2, so they are pinning rows ('+5 0 %c' at into 1, '++5 0 %c' at into 2).
A '+-+5 0 %c' row at into 2 (and its twin) was added beyond the listed set. It kills the mutant that drops '-' from the scan's set; no other row tells it apart.

The fix commit carries the rewritten comment above the reached test and the new helper's XML doc, as 13e5021 did for its own change, so that it does not ship a comment the code makes false. Every other text is in the docs commit.

'No digits there tells nothing' is implemented by the lookup missing, not by an explicit digit test. _sectionDigitsAt holds only positions of digits, and -1, which no place equals, so a lookup at a sign or at the x of xref finds nothing. An explicit test would add only an equivalent mutant.

'The run reaching the end of the bytes searched tells nothing' is kept as the defensive arm `signs < 0 ? at`, with the place being a sign there. No input reaches it: C2 and C5 are equivalent and line 5554 is partial in coverage.

A place before the bytes searched is not guarded in DigitsPastSigns. Its parameter says the place lies within the bytes searched, and the comment above the reached test says why: a replaced candidate, the start of the stream an /XRefStm read, is takeAt or in _sectionsReadAt, and the earlier conjuncts settle it before the digits are looked up.

RecordSectionReached's remark is unchanged. It says what is recorded and why a section reached at a sign is a stream with its digits, not where the digits are looked up, and it stays true. validation-rules.md row 56, lazy-reading.md around lines 212 and 262, and the line-test clauses of diagnostics.md rows 110 and 116 are unchanged: their qualifiers belong to the line test and the passed-over record, which this change does not touch.
One paragraph of TryRelocateXRefSection's remark was wrapped again: a7bcdc6 had left one overlong line there.
The #327 comment measures the two files the previous #327 comment measured, described in words and not named.
